basis: Direct pixels, each original opened once before drawing. No modern image inspected.

observations: One vertical diagram, eye above and object below. Rounded eye outline has a distinct lower entrance and elongated eye-lens shape.

An axial line runs through the eye and past the lower object endpoint. An oblique solid line runs from the left object endpoint toward the eye entrance and continues inside to the opposite retinal side; an arrow on its external part points toward the eye.
The short object interval crosses from the left endpoint to the axis and is labelled h. The exterior axial distance is bracketed on the right and labelled d0.
The exterior wedge between oblique line and axis is labelled phi. Inside the eye an axial and oblique line bound a small unlabelled retinal interval.
No named points, numerical tick values, grid, panel subdivisions or instrument lens outside the eye are visible.
One vertical diagram, eye above, object below, and a horizontal double outward-arrow lens symbol between them. Rounded eye outline has a distinct entrance and eye-lens shape.
An axial line runs from the lower object base through the instrument centre into the eye.
The short lower object interval is labelled h. The axial object-to-instrument interval is bracketed at the right and labelled F.

Two solid incident paths start at the same left object endpoint, one toward the instrument centre and the other toward an off-axis instrument intercept. Direction arrows point toward the instrument and eye.
Above the instrument the two paths run as a near-axis parallel bundle into the eye, then meet at an off-axis retinal location. An axial reference continues to the opposite eye boundary.
Phi1 appears twice, at the incident-side wedge and the emergent-side wedge relative to the axis. No numerical focal length, named point labels, grid or second panel is present.

modernAdditions: Rotate the optical arrangement to a horizontal object-left, eye-right frame without changing optical order.
Use the existing d693 eye-outline path as identification-only anatomy, not as a source-mathematics assertion.
Use clean dimension caps rather than scanned braces; preserve h, d0 and F meanings.
Regularize the instrument as a thin converging lens with two outward arrowheads, and its ray bundle as exactly parallel in the paraxial model.
Hidden construction points, exact equal-radius angle endpoints and direction arrows support executable assertions; their coordinates are schematic, not physical centimetres.
The eye-internal rays are schematic. A relaxed eye is claimed only for an appropriate eye state receiving the magnifier's parallel bundle; unaided viewing at d0 is not labelled relaxed.
